newsitem.title: USA: Sharp launches wide-screen format notebooks.
newsitem.headline: Sharp launches wide-screen format notebooks.

text.p: Sharp Electronics Corp. Tuesday launched WideNote, the first line of notebook computers with a wide-screen format.

The liquid crystal display screens have the same proportions as a movie theatre screen, measuring 9.625 inches wide by 5.625 high. They measure 11.28 inches diagonally, compared with 11 inches for a regular notebook computer.

The wide screen allows users to view two Web pages or two Microsoft Corp. Windows applications simultaneously, Sharp said. They also allow for minimal side-to-side scrolling when viewing landscape-mode applications, such as spreadsheets.
The WideNote screen is also 50 percent brighter than displays on typical notebook personal computers, the company said.
WideNote weighs about 4.6 pounds and takes up less space than a standard letter-sized pad, Sharp said.
The notebooks should be available in early October, selling at about $2,999 to $3,499, Sharp said.
Sharp Electronics, based in Mahwah, N.J., is the U.S. sales and marketing subsidiary of Japan's Sharp Corp.
